questions.q: On page 158, what is the treatment ('Rx') for patients with EITHER '2. Interim PET with Deauville score : 3, 4, 5' OR '3. Relapsed refractory (R/r) HD'?
opts: Continue 2 additional cycles of low-dose ABVD alone without stem cell transplantation
Oral maintenance methotrexate + 6-mercaptopurine for 2–3 years
Salvage chemotherapy + Autologous stem cell transplant
Involved-field radiotherapy monotherapy without systemic chemotherapy
questions.exp: Items 2 and 3 on page 158 are joined by a brace: '[2. Interim PET with Deauville score : 3,4,5 + 3. Relapsed refractory (R/r) HD] → Rx : Salvage chemotherapy + Autologous stem cell transplant.' (Book p158)

questions.q: At the bottom of page 158, what are the target and indications of Brentuximab, the indication for BEACOPP, and the two rules for Involved site/field radiotherapy?
opts: Brentuximab: BCL-2 oral inhibitor; BEACOPP regime: pediatric maintenance regimen; Radiotherapy: never combined with ABVD
Brentuximab: Anti-CD20 for early NLPHD only; BEACOPP regime: for Stage IA asymptomatic disease; Radiotherapy: mandatory first-line monotherapy for all Stage IV HD
Brentuximab: Bispecific anti-CD19/CD3 engager; BEACOPP regime: for AIHA complications only; Radiotherapy: contraindicated in LPHD
Brentuximab: Anti-CD30 for Refractory HD and Advanced HD; BEACOPP regime: for advanced disease; Involved site/field radiotherapy: not used except in LPHD, and can be given with ABVD

questions.sec: Chemotherapy Response by Subtype, ABVD Toxicity Table, Deauville PET-Adapted Protocol, Brentuximab, BEACOPP & ISRT
questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with a mediastinal mass causing mild dyspnea, painless rubbery left supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, and night sweats. Excisional biopsy shows collagen-banded nodules containing CD15+, CD30+ lacunar cells. After 2 cycles of ABVD, interim FDG-PET scan shows persistent high FDG avidity with a Deauville score of 4. Based on pages 156 and 158, what subtype does she have and what is the next management step?
opts: Nodular lymphocyte predominant Hodgkin's disease (CD20+ popcorn cells); treat with involved-node radiation monotherapy alone
Nodular sclerosis classical Hodgkin's disease; switch to Salvage chemotherapy + Autologous stem cell transplant (with Anti-CD30 Brentuximab indicated in refractory/advanced HD)
Early favourable PET-negative Hodgkin's disease; administer 2 more cycles of ABVD and stop all therapy
Mixed cellularity Hodgkin's disease with Deauville score 1; stop ABVD immediately without further therapy
questions.exp: Page 156 links mediastinal node + young females + lacunar cells to Nodular sclerosis classical HD (CD15+, CD30+), and page 158 specifies that 'Interim PET with Deauville score : 3,4,5' is managed with 'Salvage chemotherapy + Autologous stem cell transplant', with Anti-CD30 Brentuximab indicated for refractory/advanced HD. (Book p158)

questions.sec: Chemotherapy Response by Subtype, ABVD Toxicity Table, Deauville PET-Adapted Protocol, Brentuximab, BEACOPP & ISRT
questions.q: Which statement regarding Hodgkin's Disease management on page 158 is TRUE?
opts: False — Brentuximab is an anti-CD30 monoclonal antibody agent indicated for refractory Hodgkin's disease and advanced Hodgkin's disease
True — In the ABVD regimen, Adriamycin causes cardiotoxicity, Bleomycin causes lung fibrosis, and Vinblastine causes peripheral neuropathy
False — The BEACOPP chemotherapy regimen is used for advanced Hodgkin's disease
True — Interim PET Deauville scores of 3, 4, or 5 indicate complete metabolic remission requiring no further chemotherapy
questions.exp: All four lines appear directly on page 158: Adriamycin → Cardiotoxicity, Bleomycin → Lung fibrosis, Vinblastine → Peripheral neuropathy; Deauville 1–2 is PET-negative whereas Deauville 3, 4, 5 requires salvage chemotherapy + autologous stem cell transplant; Brentuximab is anti-CD30 for refractory & advanced HD; BEACOPP is for advanced disease. (Book p158)

units.title: Germinal-Centre Physiology Diagram, B-Cell Tumor Origin Table & NF-κB (NK-κβ) Pathogenesis
units.sec: Germinal-Centre Physiology Diagram, B-Cell Tumor Origin Table & NF-κB (NK-κβ) Pathogenesis
units.guide:
GC physiology: Pre-GC → Germinal center [Dark Zone (Centroblasts) + Light Zone (Centrocytes)] → Post-GC → Memory B-cells, and Light Zone downward → Plasmablasts → Plasma cells.
Origin table: Centrocytes → Follicular lymphoma; Pre-GC → MCL; Centroblasts → DLBCL & Burkitt's; Post-GC → MZL; Plasmablast → ABC-DLBCL; Plasma cells → Multiple myeloma; Memory B cells → SLL, Waldenström's, Hairy cell leukemia.
Hodgkin pathogenesis: Upregulation of NF-κB [printed NK-κβ] seen; M > F.

units.title: Dark-Zone Origin & Chr 9 PDL1 Aberration, Stage Cure Rates, HL vs NHL Comparison Table & Pel-Ebstein Fever
units.sec: Dark-Zone Origin & Chr 9 PDL1 Aberration, Stage Cure Rates, HL vs NHL Comparison Table & Pel-Ebstein Fever
units.guide:
Origin & cure rates: Dark-zone GC B-cells undergo somatic hypermutation → cells slated for apoptosis acquire PDL1 gene aberration (chr 9) → ↓ apoptosis → Hodgkin's disease. Cure rates: Early favorable (I/II) >90%, Early unfavorable (I/II) ≥85%, Advanced (III/IV) ~80%.
HL vs NHL: HL = good survival, bimodal (m/c 15–34 yrs, 2nd peak >60 yrs), nodal, paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration, B-symptoms in 30%, contiguous spread ⊕, EBV ⊕⊕⊕; NHL = >60 yrs, extranodal (m/c GIT, Waldeyer's ring), contiguous spread ⊖, EBV ⊕.
Pel-Ebstein fever: Low-grade irregular cyclical fever that spikes gradually and alternates with afebrile intervals.

units.title: Reed-Sternberg Cell Morphology, NLPHD vs Classical HD Classification (Worldwide vs India) & Comparison Table
units.sec: Reed-Sternberg Cell Morphology, NLPHD vs Classical HD Classification (Worldwide vs India) & Comparison Table
units.guide:
RS cell: Bilobed nucleus, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli separated by clear space from nuclear membrane; specific for HL only if inflammatory background +ve.
Classification: Nodular LP-HD = benign entity, excellent prognosis, axillary node, Rx radiation of involved node; Classical HD = LR, LD, Nodular sclerosis (NS — m/c worldwide), Mixed cellularity (MC — m/c in India).
Classical vs Nodular table: Classical = CD15+, CD30+, B symptoms ⊕, EBV ⊕ (100/70/40/20: LD 100%, MC 70%, NS 40%, LR 20%), Histology (LD: RS absent [printed], MC: classical RS, NS: lacunar RS, LR: paucity of RS); Nodular = CD20+, CD45+, Surface Ig+, B symptoms absent, EBV ⊖, Popcorn RS / L&H cells.

units.title: EBV/ALCL Recap Notes, Hodgkin Clinical Features, Paraneoplastic Syndromes & NS vs MC Subtype Profiles
units.sec: EBV/ALCL Recap Notes, Hodgkin Clinical Features, Paraneoplastic Syndromes & NS vs MC Subtype Profiles
units.guide:
Recap notes: EBV-associated NHL includes endemic Burkitt's, post-transplant & primary CNS (DLBCL), and extranodal NK/T-lymphoma (very poor prognosis, nasal mass); ALCL = CD30+, hallmark & flower cells.
Clinical features: Diffuse painless rubbery firm lymphadenopathy — Posterior cervical (60–80%) > Supraclavicular > Axillary (NLPHD); B symptoms (30–40%), M>F, alcohol-induced ↑ size in node, unexplained pruritus, diagnostic Pel-Ebstein fever.
Paraneoplastic & subtypes: Subacute cerebellar degeneration, minimal change disease, cholangitis, vanishing bile duct syndrome. NS = mediastinal mass, young females, SVC obstruction, pleural effusion, lacunar cells; MC = HIV+, 70% EBV+ (also LD), extensive B symptoms, elderly/children, classical RS + mononuclear cells.

units.title: Richter Recap, Staging Workup (Excision Biopsy & FDG-PET), Unfavourable Criteria & β2-Microglobulin Note
units.sec: Richter Recap, Staging Workup (Excision Biopsy & FDG-PET), Unfavourable Criteria & β2-Microglobulin Note
units.guide:
Staging workup: Full thickness excision biopsy (IOC); FDG-PET scan = single most valuable test for staging. Ann-Arbor I–IV with A (no B symptoms) / B (B symptoms +ve).
Early (I–II) Unfavorable criteria: Age >60, B symptoms +ve, Bulky nodes (>10 cm), ≥4 extranodal sites [printed], ESR ≥50 mm/hr.
Other paraneoplastic & lab markers: ↑↑ LDH, hypercalcemia, hypoglycemia, hyponatremia; Beta-2 microglobulin indicates poor prognosis in CLL, HD, and MM.

units.title: Chemotherapy Response by Subtype, ABVD Toxicity Table, Deauville PET-Adapted Protocol, Brentuximab, BEACOPP & ISRT
units.sec: Chemotherapy Response by Subtype, ABVD Toxicity Table, Deauville PET-Adapted Protocol, Brentuximab, BEACOPP & ISRT
units.guide:
Chemo response & ABVD toxicities: MC & LD = poor response, NS = very good, LR = excellent. ABVD: Adriamycin (cardiotoxicity), Bleomycin (lung fibrosis), Vinblastine (peripheral neuropathy), Dacarbazine (–).
Deauville 5-point PET protocol (after 2 cycles ABVD): Deauville 1–2 → +2 cycles (early favourable), +3 cycles [printed] (early unfavourable), +4 cycles (advanced disease); Deauville 3,4,5 OR relapsed/refractory HD → Salvage chemo + Autologous stem cell transplant.
Targeted & RT notes: Brentuximab (anti-CD30) for refractory & advanced HD; BEACOPP for advanced disease; ISRT/IFRT not used alone except in LPHD, can be combined with ABVD.
